question: Find the circumference (in m) of the largest circle that can be drawn completely inside a rectangle whose dimensions are given as 126 m and 226 m. (Take π = (22)/(7))
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Diameter of the largest circle in a rectangle = Breadth of the rectangle = 126 m.

Circumference = π × d

⇒ 22/7 × 126

⇒ 396 m

**∴ The correct answer is 396 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the rectangle = 226 m

Breadth of the rectangle = 126 m

 
 
 
• 
 
 226 m
 126 m
 d = 126 m

**Formula Used:**

Circumference of a circle = 2 × π × r

**Calculations:**

⇒ For the largest circle to be completely inside the rectangle, its diameter must be equal to the smaller side (breadth) of the rectangle.

⇒ Diameter of the circle (d) = 126 m

⇒ Radius (r) = d ÷ 2 = 126 ÷ 2 = 63 m

⇒ Circumference = 2 × (22/7) × 63

⇒ Circumference = 2 × 22 × 9

⇒ Circumference = 44 × 9 = 396 m

**∴ The correct answer is 396 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Largest Circle inside a Rectangle

The diameter is always equal to the shorter side (breadth) of the rectangle.

Largest Circle inside a Square

The diameter is equal to the side of the square. Area = π × (a/2)².

Largest Square inside a Circle

The diagonal of the square is equal to the diameter of the circle. Side = d ÷ √2.
